svg.title: Five stages run from chosen project folders through an offline scan, optional advisory lookups and a graph dashboard to a policy result and candidate events.
svg.desc: Moving figure, 10 seconds, looping, no sound. 1. TRIUNA LABS, INC. · SUPPLY CHAIN GRAPH. From selected folders to evidence. What the public skill and local starter do today. Marked CURRENT WORKFLOW. Footer: Triuna Labs, Inc. · Public reusable skill · Real snapshots and dashboards stay private. 2. 01 · CHOOSE: Project roots. Add a folder with the native picker in local serve mode, paste a path, or run bounded discovery. Commands: init · set-root; discover · serve. No whole-computer search. 3. 02 · COLLECT: Offline scan. Read manifests, npm or pnpm locks, source imports, Git, actions, and Python requirements. Commands: scan → snapshot.json. No install or remote fetch. 4. 03 · CHECK (OPTIONAL): Advisory data. Query OSV for resolved npm versions; query npm metadata for deprecation and latest tag. Commands: enrich · details. Shares package names. 5. 04 · EXPLORE: Graph dashboard. Four graph lenses and a start-here panel; what was read, what stayed local, which npm checks never ran. Commands: render · serve. Inspect paths and gaps. 6. 05 · EVALUATE: Policy + events. Apply a versioned policy: freshness, six coverage states, stable IDs. Compare with a chosen baseline. No alerts sent. Commands: evaluate · diff. Unknown is not clean. 7. HOW TO READ THE RESULT. A supported resolved path. 8. A chain: Project, leading to declared request, leading to locked occurrence, leading to versioned artifact. 9. Edges retain scope and file evidence; shared artifacts do not erase per-project paths.. 10. An unknown stays unknown. 11. A chain: Project, leading to source import, with nothing to establish the link to installed version: unknown. 12. No lockfile, unsupported format, failed lookup, or partial scan. States: unqueried · failed · unsupported · stale.. A source import alone does not prove an installed version or vulnerability status..
